You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: arc-demo-rule-inference
description: Use when inferring ARC transformations from demonstrations.
---

# ARC demonstration-driven rule inference

Use for ARC tasks where a test grid is accompanied by one or more demonstrations. Infer a transformation that generalizes, rather than matching a visual hunch.

## Procedure

1. **Parse the full instance.** Record dimensions, distinct colors, repeated backgrounds, exceptional shapes/markers, and any action/attempt/demo caps. Keep row/column coordinates explicit and use them consistently.
2. **Compare each demo cell-by-cell.** Align input and output at matching coordinates when dimensions match. List changed coordinates and their before/after colors; separately note additions, removals, recolorings, dimension changes, and preserved seed structures. If dimensions differ, identify segmentation or object-count mappings that explain the change.
3. **Form a small set of competing rules.** Consider geometry, relative position, orientation, counts, symmetry, lines/regions, and transparency. Do not infer an anchor, target color, or direction solely from visual resemblance.
4. **Replay candidates on the demo.** Apply each candidate to the full demo input and compare every output cell and dimension exactly. Reject rules that leave changes unexplained or predict changes in preserved cells. All demos should fit one rule, aside from supported parameter changes such as color or size.
5. **Use demonstrations economically.** A demo request has a cost. Request one only when a specific unresolved ambiguity could materially change the test output. First extract all constraints from existing examples and test concrete hypotheses; do not request merely because the rule is not immediately obvious.
6. **Apply the validated rule to the test.** Preserve unrelated cells unless demonstrations show otherwise. Verify bounds, row and column counts, allowed values, and output dimensions before submission.

## Unresolved selective-object recoloring stream task task-4902da4a
This task family has varied grid sizes and palettes; each demo output is same dimensions and differs by recoloring a localized connected object/component, while many other objects and even same-color components stay untouched. Never use global palette substitution or infer a fixed target/replacement color. Observed demo changes (1-indexed): pair 1, a 3-cell color-4 object at rows 2-3, cols 24-25 becomes 9; pair 2, a 4-cell color-9 object at rows 5-7, cols 19-20 becomes 0; pair 3, one color-8 cell at row 25, col 12 becomes 9; pair 4, a vertical three-cell color-4 object at rows 19-21, col 4 becomes 1; pair 5, three adjacent color-9 cells at row 5, cols 2-4 become 8; pair 6, the connected color-9 object around rows 6-11, cols 7-10 becomes 0; pair 7, the isolated color-0 cell at row 4, col 15 becomes 2; pair 8, the small color-5 component at rows 9-12, cols 16-17 becomes 8. The common selector/replacement mechanism was not identified from these examples; these local recolorings do not establish a simple color, size, edge, or line-alignment rule. In this task attempt, eight demos were exhausted and all eight test submissions were incorrect. The submitted guesses variously recolored test color-5 motifs or isolated cells to 1, 6, or 8, and finally changed an isolated 0 to 2; none are supported by the demonstrations. Future instances should first build a complete connected-component table for every demo (changed and preserved objects, colors, silhouette, area, location, adjacency and possible paired objects), test a selector and output-color key that explains every pair, and avoid submitting without a rule that replays all examples. This note is a cautionary unresolved case, not a validated rule.

## Confirmed denoising variant: task-16b1bf1f
Images are mostly solid/rectangular coherent regions on a dominant background, with isolated one-cell foreign-color noise and occasional notches in a coherent shape. Clean by changing every isolated anomalous pixel to the underlying region color if it lies inside/on a coherent object; otherwise change it to the background. Preserve coherent regions even when their color is uncommon. Do not globally substitute palette colors, and do not assume the outlier's color predicts its destination.

First demo (22x25, background 4) confirms: remove isolated noise of colors 1,6,7 at coordinates (0-indexed) (0,6),(0,24),(2,0),(2,24),(1,12),(4,13),(4,21),(8,0),(9,21),(10,1),(10,3),(12,7),(12,10),(12,18),(11,21),(15,10),(16,5),(17,7),(21,9); each becomes its local coherent-region/background color. Also fill the anomalous notch (15,10) in a 3-region to 3. Retain solid coherent 3 and 5 objects and small 2x2/rectangular forms, including apparently unusual components. This rule was independently confirmed in three earlier demos: demo 1 (27x10, bg1) removed scattered colors 0/2/3/8/9 and restored cells inside color-6 forms to 6; demo 2 (13x28, bg5) removed singleton intrusions 1/6/9 in coherent color-4 and color-2 regions; demo 3 (12x26, bg5) removed isolated 2/3/4/6 artifacts while preserving coherent 7/8/9 structures.

The accepted test output for the 18x24 grid retained coherent color-5 and color-9 regions plus coherent color-8/9 blocks. It corrected isolated noise as follows (0-indexed): (0,1) 8→2; (2,12) 4→2; (3,2) 1→2; (4,5) 6→2; (7,7) 6→2; (7,20) 4→2; (8,3) 4→2; (8,9) 8→2; (9,14) 4→2; (9,17) 0→2; (9,23) 0→2; (10,4) 3→5; (10,7) 6→5; (10,9) 6→2; (10,16) 6→2; (10,21) 4→2; (13,4) 3→5; (14,11) 8→2; (16,11) 4→9; (16,23) 6→2; (17,1) 6→2. Notably, row 3 col 2 (value 1) and row 10 col 4/value3 and row13 col4/value3 were restored differently according to whether they intrude on a coherent region or lie at its boundary/background. Previous guesses that changed coherent-block extents or left artifacts untouched were wrong. Use local underlying structure and exact changed/preserved audit; validate every cell of the proposed output. Preserve connected/block-shaped objects such as the 1 regions and 8 forms.

## Unresolved split-panel reduction: task-9a9d9fc4
A distinct instance had a full-height divider column (color 2) separating 10×27 and 10×27 panels; another demo had a full-width divider row (color 9) separating two 5×14 panels. Outputs were 27×10 and 5×14 respectively, i.e. one panel-sized output, predominantly color 4 with sparse color-3 cells. Inputs used panel colors {8,4} and {7,4} in the vertical-separator demo, and {5,4} above / {2,4} below in the horizontal-separator demo. Test was 18×23 with a full-height color-8 divider at column 11, panels 18×11 using {0,6} and {0,9}; likely output shape 18×11. Eight test submissions all failed. Guesses that treated one panel as a direct binary mask, guessed 3/4 cellwise patterns, or used unrelated hand-built marker placements were not validated. Do not reuse any guessed test grid or assume which half controls the sparse 3s. On recurrence, align both panels to the output, tabulate all coordinates for each input color and each output color in both demos, and test a joint positional relation (including flips/rotations, overlap, and counts) against every output cell before submitting. The rule remains unresolved.
7. **Follow the interface exactly.** In ARC stream tasks requiring a final-line JSON action, emit exactly one valid action object on the last line, without explanatory prose.

## Recurring binary-noise palette remapping case
A Continual-ARC instance with dense binary noise on 9/5 was solved by a whole-grid color substitution: every 9 became 0 and every 5 became 9. Its confirming small demo had a 14x5 grid of 9s with one 5; output changed every 9 to 0 and the lone 5 to 9. An earlier demo in the same instance used colors 5/7 and mapped 5→7, 7→0, so do not assume a fixed mapping from color identity alone across palette variants; derive the mapping from the instance's demonstrations and verify it applies globally to every cell. Prior incorrect attempts came from reversing/guessing the 5/9 mapping. For this demonstrated 5/9 variant, use 9→0 and 5→9.

## Confirmed recurring case: task-5c4cb9ae (18x18 to 6x6 mini-grid)
Partition the input into a regular grid of 3x3 tiles (not 6x6 tiles). Emit one output cell per tile, preserving tile row/column order. For each tile, ignore background/noise colors 0 and 5; if any other color is present, output that color, otherwise output 0. The demonstrated/test instance had a sole color-4 motif confined to the top-left 6x6 region: it landed in output tile row 0, column 1, producing [[0,4,0,0,0,0], then five all-zero rows]. This was accepted. An initial wrong attempt used 6x6 tiles and produced a 3x3 grid, so carefully distinguish tile size from output dimensions: 18x18 becomes 6x6 via 3x3 tiles. Validate all tile cells, including multi-color exceptional cells if present; the known instance only had color 4 among colors other than 0/5.

## Verified recurring case: task-a613028a (3x2 mirror tiling)
This task family expands any HxW input into a 3H x 2W output by mirror-tiling the original grid. For the demo 3x13 -> 9x26, each source row is expanded horizontally as `reverse(row) + row`; vertically the rows follow `[r3,r2,r1, r1,r2,r3, r3,r2,r1]`. This corresponds to three alternating mirrored row blocks. Equivalently, output `[R][C] = input[vertical_source(R)][horizontal_source(C)]`, with horizontal indices `W-1..0, 0..W-1`; vertical indices `H-1..0, 0..H-1, H-1..0`. Expanded dimensions are 3H by 2W. A separate accepted instance of this task id had a 2x14 test and 6x28 output, consistent with the same dimensional rule. Validate every output row length and total row count before submission; in a 10x14 test, expected dimensions are 30x28. Prior attempt grids for the 10x14 test were malformed (wrong row lengths and/or count) as well as not reliable evidence of a rule failure; the mirror-tiling rule itself matches the demo exactly. The accepted example from the related run was for input `[[2,7,2,2,7,7,2,7,2,2,2,0,2,2],[0,0,7,7,7,7,2,2,7,7,7,2,0,7]]`, output dimensions 6x28.

This task family can change dimensions substantially and is not a same-size recoloring. Do not overfit output dimensions to the demo; apply the 3H x 2W rule and audit exact coordinates, all rows, and all columns.


## Additional task-21fede32 run (unresolved; do not treat guesses as rules)
A separate 14x23 test instance used 8 demos and all 8 submissions failed. All pairs retained dimensions and changed one connected component, but a selector/recolor mapping was not established. Demo changed component → replacement (coordinates 1-indexed):
1. Input 28x16, bg0, color2 separator L at col5 rows1-9 and row9 cols1-5: color5 component rows17-19 cols5-6, silhouette 5/55/05 →2. Many other 5 components unchanged.
2. Input 16x25, bg3, color8 separator L at col4 rows1-4 and row4 cols1-4: isolated 1 at row11 col4 →8. Other 1,6,7,2,9,5 objects unchanged.
3. Input 26x10, bg9, color5 separator L at col5 rows1-6 and row6 cols1-5: color1 component rows11-13 cols4-6 →5. Other objects unchanged.
4. Input 25x27, bg5, color7 separator L at col19 rows1-5 and row5 cols19-27: color2 upper-right component rows6-8 cols21-25 →7. Other color2 and colored objects unchanged.
5. Input 17x21, bg3, no obvious large divider: color4 vertical triplet at col12 rows8-10 →0. Other color4 objects unchanged.
6. Input 15x24, bg8, color0 separator L at col17 rows1-6 and row6 cols17-24: isolated 6 at row8 col17 →0. Other 6 objects unchanged.
7. Input 21x19, bg7, no obvious divider: color5 component (four horizontal at row5 cols5-8 plus one below at row6 col6) →1. Other 5 absent; color8 and 1 objects unchanged.
8. Input 21x28, bg5, color3 separator L at col6 rows1-6 and row6 cols1-6: color4 upper-right component rows7-9 cols16-19 (11 cells) →3. Similar lower-right 4 component unchanged.
The demos suggest some selected object might relate spatially to a separator or another component, but demos 5 and 7 lack an obvious separator and counterexamples remain. Replacement often equals separator color when a divider exists, but this is not universal. Never generalize from a single motif; test a candidate against all changed and preserved components.
The test grid for that instance had upper objects color1 at rows1-3 cols2 and 20-21; color9 col6 rows1-2 plus left region rows6-10 cols3-4 and row6 cols7-12; color3 objects row3 col7, rows4 col6-7, line col15 rows7-10, pair row7 cols14-15, pair row11 cols5-6, row12 cols11-14; color6 cluster rows2-4 cols13-17; 4 at row3 col11 and pair row10 cols21-22; color5 object rows11-12 cols19-23/19; color7 block rows13-14 cols21-23. Failed output hypotheses were: change color6 cluster to3; additionally change color7 block to9; change color3 vertical line to9; change color7 block to3; change isolated 4 to9; change color7 block to9 again; change color3 vertical object to4; then change isolated 4 and color7 block to9; final submitted variations changing the color3 line and/or isolated 4/color7 cluster. These failures reject those particular predictions, not necessarily each individual component choice in every combination. Current rule unresolved.

## Diagonal-ray task task-9bc5df6e: distinguish ray direction and blockers
This task ID has at least two observed variants; don't blindly reuse a previous test grid or assume every run extends to the boundary. In the prior confirmed run, colored diagonal seed pairs/branches extended in a straight diagonal ray away from the local motif through background cells to the boundary, preserving seed cells and unrelated content. In a separate run, demos showed background-only diagonal rays, but the accepted test was unchanged: its color-3 pair at (0,3),(1,4) had a southeast continuation landing on non-background color 2 at (2,5), and no cells were changed. This supports extending only through background and stopping before any non-background cell, rather than overwriting blockers; the opposite ray from the upper seed was out of bounds. Preserve all motif cells and foreign-color blockers. Infer ray direction from the outward-facing endpoint(s), not merely from a pair's slope, and check the next ray cell before filling. The separate run's demos: demo 1 (26x24, bg8) extended color 7 southwest from (13,9) to the boundary, retaining the multicolor seed motif; demo 2 (25x25, bg0) extended color 6 northwest from (13,7) to the boundary, retaining the seed pair and adjacent colors 5,2,3. The current test's unchanged output was accepted. Keep the background-only stopping detail scoped to evidence; do not assume a blocker is overwritten.

Three demonstrations in the earlier run establish a recurring diagonal-ray construction: colored diagonal seed pairs/branches extend in a straight diagonal ray away from the local motif until the grid boundary, preserving all seed cells and unrelated content. Infer the direction from the motif's outward-facing endpoint(s), not merely from a pair's slope; directions can differ for separate rays. Demo 1 (23x8, bg5): color-3 pair (0-indexed rows 7,8; cols 1,2) extends from (7,1) NW to (6,0); color-2 pair at (7,4),(8,3) extends from (7,4) NE through (6,5),(5,6),(4,7). The color-8 motif remains unchanged. Demo 2 (19x28, bg7): the color-9 branched shape has outward lower-left and lower-right diagonal arms; extend from (3,5) SW through (4,4),(5,3),(6,2),(7,1),(8,0), and from (3,8) SE through (4,9) ... (17,22) and (18,23), preserving the original shape. Demo 3 (24x26, bg8): color-3 pair (1,16),(2,17) extends NW by adding (0,15); all other colors/shapes remain unchanged. The accepted test for the instance had background 9 and color-6 diagonal pair (3,14),(4,13); the ray continues NE from (3,14), adding (2,15),(1,16),(0,17), with all other cells preserved. Two earlier incorrect test submissions both extended the 6 pair SW from its lower endpoint (and omitted the actual NE ray), confirming direction must be selected from the outward endpoint/direction indicated by the motif. On recurrence, identify the diagonal branch endpoints and extend only the outward-facing rays to the boundary; avoid blanket extension in both directions unless a demo supports it. Validate coordinates and preserve the seed/multicolor motifs exactly.

## Common pitfalls

- Treating a plausible motif match as proof: reproduce the demo output cell-for-cell first.
- Assuming the most common color is always background or target.
- Assuming markers are anchors, centers, or replacement cells without output evidence.
- Ignoring remote-row/column changes or whether the seed motif remains unchanged.
- Submitting a guessed output after an unverified hypothesis; use a demo if it resolves an important ambiguity at acceptable cost.
- Spending actions on unrelated tools or repeated planning that does not reduce uncertainty. In strict action interfaces, the required response is the task action itself.

## Confirmed task-a8c517ee variant: fill enclosed frame interiors by parity
Outlined rectangular/square frames retain their borders while every enclosed background cell is filled. Fill color is 2 when both interior dimensions are even; otherwise use 7. Examples include 2x2 and 6x6 interiors→2, and 5x5, 5x7, 3x3, and 1x1→7. Preserve all unrelated cells and frame borders; infer frames regardless of border color. A confirmed recurrence had color-4 frame with a 2x2 interior→2, color-1 frame with 5x5→7, and color-8 frame with 1x1→7. Another accepted 15x20 test filled the color-4 frame's 6x6 hole with 2, color-5 frame's 3x3 with 7, and color-6 frame's 1x1 with 7. A further demo had 3-frame 2x2→2, 6-frame 2x2→2, and 1-frame 1x1→7. Pitfall: fill the entire interior rectangle, including its last/lowest interior row; an initial wrong submission omitted that row in one 3x3 interior even though the parity/color rule was correct. Validate each frame's interior bounds from the border coordinates and audit all interior cells before submitting. Do not fill frame borders or globally recolor frame colors.

## task-ebb0e4e4 recurrence: horizontal pattern continuation; beware generated variants

### Separate eight-demo unresolved run (2026-09)
Do not confuse this instance with the accepted contiguous row-tail or alternating-motif variants below. Eight demos were exhausted; six valid-shaped test submissions (the first was malformed) were wrong, and the selector/extent of changed rightward tails remained unresolved. The recurring visible operation is changing some right-tail/background cells to 1 while preserving patterned cells, but choosing the affected row and exact continuation pattern is critical. Demo evidence (0-indexed):

1. 19x12, bg9/pattern8: row2 had 8 at cols0–2 then 9 tail cols3–11→1; row17 had 8 cols0–5 then 9 tail cols6–11→1. Full 8 rows9 and13 unchanged.
2. 30x20, bg9/pattern8: row0 had 8 cols0–3, then 9 tail cols4–19→1; full 8 row20 unchanged.
3. 20x11, bg8/pattern0: row8 had 0 cols0–6 then 8 tail cols7–10→1; full 0 row14 unchanged.
4. 9x19, bg3/pattern8: only row8's final two cells (cols17–18, both 3) became 1; nearby rows include alternating 8/3 patterns and row8 has an irregular mostly-8 run. Do not fill its whole apparent tail.
5. 15x14, bg6/pattern2: row6 cols9–13 (6 tail after 6s then 2s)→1; row10 col13 (6)→1 after a run of 6 then 2. Full rows5 and9 unchanged; row11 has a 2 run ending before a single bg6, unchanged.
6. 21x17, bg8/pattern7: row13-14 cols12–16 (8s after 7 blocks)→1; row15's alternating tail at cols12,14,16 became 1 while 8 at cols13,15 remained. Other partial 7 shapes and row3 alternating 7/8 unchanged.
7. 14x26, bg8/pattern7: row11 col25 (8)→1 after a 7 run cols0–24; full 7 row3 unchanged.
8. 29x26, bg4/pattern8: row16 col25 (4)→1 after an 8 run cols0–24; full 8 rows5 and23 unchanged.

The commonality suggests a horizontal continuation/difference-to-1 task, often on a partial patterned row with an exemplar elsewhere, but the exact selection rule is not determined by simple partial-run detection: demo 1–3 have two changed tails, demos 7–8 one endpoint, demo4 only last two cells, and demo6 changes selected alternating tail positions. Preserve all unselected rows and matching pattern-phase cells. Build explicit row/run and motif correspondences and replay every changed and unchanged case before any test attempt. The test had three sparse patterned bands (rows 1–3, 8–10, 20–22; colors 2/3). Guesses that blanket-filled tails of rows 1,2,3,8,9,10,20,21,22 or changed selected endpoint/alternating cells at guessed locations all failed; none are evidence for the true rule. In a recurrence, avoid recycling those guesses; analyze row/column pattern registration from scratch.

# ARC grid rule inference under action constraints

Use this class-level workflow for ARC/Continual-ARC puzzles with demonstrations and a limited number of submissions or demo requests.

## Confirmed panel-template replication variant: task-8e04f0ad
Full-width/full-height separator lines of color 9 partition the grid into equal rectangular panels. One panel contains a pattern and the other panels are blank/background; copy the source panel's pattern into every panel at the same local coordinates, preserving separator lines. Infer panel height/width from separator spacing and identify the uniquely populated source region; do not copy separator cells as part of the pattern. Demo: 6x26 with vertical color-4 separators at columns 8 and 17; the 6x8 pattern in the first panel repeated at local coordinates in the next two panels, while separator columns remained 4. Accepted test: 20x19 with color-9 separator rows 6 and 13 and column 9, dividing into 3x2 panels of 6x9 interior cells; the populated bottom-left 6x9 tile was copied into all six panels at matching local coordinates, leaving row/column separator lines unchanged. Preserve all copied colors, including 0, and preserve background cells within the source tile.

## Infer and verify
1. Parse dimensions, colors, candidate background/edge colors, markers, and action caps. Index cells consistently by row and column.
2. Compare each demo input/output at identical coordinates. Enumerate changed cells, their original and output colors, and unchanged structures. Separate marker recoloring from rays/fills and from wholesale stripe changes.
3. Maintain a small set of plausible rules. Consider orientation, anchor, extent, endpoint exclusion, target colors, and object interaction separately; do not infer from a single visual resemblance.
4. Replay every candidate on every demo cell-by-cell. Reject any rule that misses a changed cell or alters a preserved cell. A transformation is not validated merely because one part fits.
5. Apply the surviving rule to the test input, preserve unrelated cells, and validate dimensions, row lengths, bounds, and palette before submission.

## Demo/action budget
- A request costs score. Request only when a concrete ambiguity remains and explain internally which candidate rules the next example should distinguish.
- Use only actions authorized by the puzzle interface. In a submit/request_demos/finish protocol, do not call unrelated tools or task-planning actions; reason from visible grids and output only the required JSON action.
- After incorrect feedback, do not submit a near-identical grid with superficial edits. Treat the candidate rule as suspect, identify which assumptions were unproven, and reconstruct the output from the demos.
- If demos leave a behavior unresolved, do not present it as established. Seek a discriminating example only if worth its cost; otherwise make the most evidence-supported choice within the remaining attempt budget.

## Directional lines and boundary rays
For markers near edge bars, verify independently: ray direction, whether the marker becomes the ray color or a special color, where the ray stops, whether the boundary is preserved, and whether only marker-containing rows/columns activate. For diagonal rays, check each next cell: a current task-9bc5df6e run had rays extend through background to the boundary, but a test ray's next cell was a foreign non-background color and the accepted output preserved that blocker and added no ray. Thus use background-only extension when supported and never overwrite foreign-color cells without demo evidence. Other task-9bc5df6e recurrence had rays reaching boundaries; treat variant scope carefully. Do not assume opposite-edge symmetry. Special complete bands or stripes may have a separate selection rule; preserve them unless demonstrations establish how they are selected. See `references/boundary-ray-case.md` for a documented example and its limitations.

## Confirmed task-a8c517ee variant: fill enclosed frame interiors by parity
Two demos and an accepted test establish that outlined rectangular/square frames retain their borders while enclosed background cells are filled. The demonstrated outputs show fill color 2 when both interior dimensions are even (demo 2: a 2x2 hole; accepted test: a 6x6 hole), and color 7 when at least one interior dimension is odd (demo 1: 5x5; demo 2: 5x5, 5x7, 1x1, and 3x3; accepted test: 3x3 and 1x1). Other grid cells and frame borders stay unchanged. This parity mapping fits all observed cases. A further accepted 21x18 recurrence confirmed it: a color-4 frame with a 2x2 interior was filled with 2, while color-1 frame with 5x5 interior and color-8 frame with 1x1 interior were filled with 7; all frame borders and unrelated cells were preserved. Do not fill frame borders or globally recolor frame colors. Accepted test 15x20: the 4-frame at rows 0–7, cols 8–15 has 6x6 interior filled 2; the 5-frame at rows 9–13, cols 10–14 has 3x3 interior filled 7; the 6-frame at rows 10–12, cols 3–5 has its single interior cell filled 7. First submission incorrectly used 7 for the even 6x6 hole; accepted output confirms the parity mapping. A further accepted 23x22 recurrence has differently colored frames (colors 1, 4, 6, 8, 9) with 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 3x2, 4x4 interiors. Fill 2x2 and 4x4 interiors with 2 because both dimensions are even; fill the others with 7 because at least one dimension is odd. The small 3x3 outer frames with 1x1 holes also receive 7. All borders, background (3), and unrelated content remain unchanged. This additionally confirms the rule is independent of frame color and applies to rectangular holes.

## Confirmed full monochromatic line recoloring variant: task-07cb84d7
A demo and accepted test establish that identify every row and column whose cells are all the same color, then recolor those complete lines to color 2. Keep all cells outside those qualifying lines unchanged; intersections are also 2. The line color need not match between lines. In the demo (21x28), complete color-1 rows (indices 1, 4, 14) and columns (indices 0, 5) became color 2; all partial/singleton color-1 cells and color-3 cells remained as-is. In the accepted 12x8 test, complete color-5 columns 2 and 3 and complete color-5 row 9 became color 2, while other 5s and all 7s stayed unchanged. Check full-line status against the original input, not incrementally modified cells. A further accepted 15x7 recurrence confirms the rule: the all-8 rows 2 and 14 and all-8 column 0 became 2; all other cells remained unchanged, including partial 8s. A further task-07cb84d7 recurrence with background 5 and line color 9 confirmed that every fully monochromatic row or column is recolored to 2, including all qualifying lines regardless of whether there is only one or several; in that 26x23 test, full rows 9 and 25 and full columns 9, 15, 18, and 22 were the qualifying lines. Validate by enumerating every row and column against the original input before generating output—missing even one full line causes a wrong answer. The rule is line-color agnostic: demonstrations also use monochromatic lines of colors 0, 3, and 5, all recolored to 2. Preserve every cell outside qualifying lines.

## Confirmed diagonal-residue periodic fill variant: task-fce33c1b
Sparse colored straight lines encode a periodic full-grid pattern: extend each marked line's color to every line with the same residue modulo the line period, producing a full tiled diagonal/stripe pattern. Determine the invariant coordinate (for example, `r+c` for up-right diagonals, `c-r` for down-right diagonals, or `r` for horizontal stripes), identify the period from parallel marker-line offsets, and map residue classes to their colors. Fill the entire grid from that residue-to-color mapping; this is not a sparse-line extension that preserves background.

Evidence from two demos and the accepted test establishes orientation-dependent cases. Demo 1 (21x21) used anti-diagonals of constant `r+c`, period 5, with residues 0..4 mapping to `[8,3,9,4,7]`. Demo 2 (23x23) used horizontal rows with period 2, row residue 0→2 and residue 1→1. Accepted 12x12 test used down-right diagonals of constant `c-r`, period 4, with residues 0..3 mapping to `[7,6,8,2]`, yielding rows `[7,6,8,2]`, `[2,7,6,8]`, `[8,2,7,6]`, `[6,8,2,7]` repeating. Infer the line orientation from marker geometry rather than assuming one axis; use line spacing and marker colors to complete residue assignments.

## Confirmed whole-pattern translation variant: task-3c7ebef4
A single demo and multiple accepted tests establish that the complete sparse non-background pattern is translated down by exactly one row, preserving its columns and colors. The vacated top row is filled with the background color; the former last row is dropped at the boundary. Demonstrations/accepted tests included backgrounds 8, 3, and this accepted 29x23 test with background 8 and pattern color 7. Its full colored pattern shifts down one row, clipping the former last row; this was confirmed correct. Infer the uniform translation vector from input/output demos, move the entire pattern as one shape, fill exposed cells with background, and clip at the grid boundary; do not change pattern geometry or recolor it.

## Output protocol
For strict ARC streams, emit exactly one valid action JSON object on the final line and no commentary. Ensure the grid has the required shape and only integer colors 0–9.

## Confirmed separator/object packing variant: task-67762d72
A separator line of color 2 and a patterned object on one side are rearranged into an adjacent packed layout: translate the entire object pattern (including its bounding-box-relative gaps and any internal background-colored cells) toward the separator until its bounding box is immediately next to it. Then place a full line of color 8 immediately beyond the object's bbox on the far side, away from the separator. Preserve the separator, pattern colors, and all unrelated/background cells; the 8-line spans the full grid. This is bidirectional: for a horizontal separator, move an object below it upward or an object above it downward; for a vertical separator, move an object to its right leftward or an object to its left rightward. The 8-line lies just beyond the packed bbox on the side away from the separator. Demo 1: 30x22, color-2 row 8, color-9 3x2 object at rows14–16 cols5–6; moved intact to rows9–11 cols5–6, with full color-8 row 12. Demo 2: 19x19, color-2 column 2, patterned bbox rows0–4 cols8–13; translated intact left to cols3–8, with full color-8 column 9. Accepted test: 14x26, separator row0, multicomponent color-1 pattern bbox rows4–8 cols3–8; translated up to rows1–5 and full color-8 row6. All other cells stayed unchanged. A further accepted 28x18 recurrence had a vertical color-2 separator at column 6 and a solid color-9 object at rows1–13, columns11–14. The object translated intact left to columns7–10, and a full-height color-8 column was added at column11. Another accepted recurrence (24x9) had a vertical color-2 separator at column 7 and a color-0 object with bbox rows9–14, cols4–5 to its left. The object moved intact rightward to cols5–6, immediately next to the separator, and a full-height color-8 column was added at col4. Other cells stayed unchanged. These examples confirm packing preserves the object's entire bounding-box-relative pattern and its perpendicular-axis coordinates; verify that the 8-line is placed on the exposed far side, not between the object and separator. Confirm object bounds and avoid overwriting separator; preserve internal pattern exactly.

## Confirmed connector variant: task-63e6a38f
Color-2 marker cells on color-1 background are linked in straight horizontal and vertical lines: for each row and column, sort marker coordinates and recolor only the color-1 cells strictly between each consecutive pair to color 3. Keep marker endpoints, all non-gap cells, and unrelated background unchanged. No diagonal links or extension beyond the outermost marker. The demo and accepted 30x14 test both confirmed this behavior; simultaneous row/column links may cross, with linked cells color 3.

## Confirmed denoising variant: task-16b1bf1f
Three demos establish a noise-cleanup task. A dominant background surrounds coherent shapes/regions, with sparse singleton foreign-color pixels contaminating objects and background. Restore intrusions to the underlying object color or background; do not blanket erase all non-background colors. Demo1: bg1 and solid color6 shapes, noisy speckles 0/2/3/8/9; restore in-shape pixels and erase off-shape ones. Demo2: bg5, coherent color4 and color2 blocks; remove isolated 1/6/9 intrusions in blocks/background. Demo3: bg5 with coherent 7/8/9 structures; remove sparse 2/3/4/6 anomalies, preserving genuine rectangular objects. Accepted test solution kept coherent color1/color8 objects, turned speckles on objects back to object color (notably color8 object's anomalous notch at row 3 col7 0-indexed), and changed stray background specks to 0. Four guesses were wrong, mostly from failing to map speckles to either object or background precisely; distinguish structural holes/noise from intentional notches by cross-checking shape continuity and demos.

## Unresolved later run of task-21fede32
A distinct run with a 19x14 test ended with all 8 submissions wrong after 8 demos. Do not reuse a memorized answer from another run of this task id. The demos all showed a localized connected component being recolored, but neither component selection nor replacement color was resolved. Exact observed changes: demo 1, color-5 component at rows 1–3 cols 1–4 →6; demo 2, isolated 8 at (17,12)→9; demo 3, two 0 cells at row 28 cols 17–18 →4; demo 4, color-7 component row 4 cols 20–22 →8; demo 5, color-7 three-cell component rows 8–9 cols 25–26 →3; demo 6, six-cell color-2 component rows 13–15 cols 7–8 →5; demo 7, one larger color-8 component in central-lower area →7; demo 8, adjacent color-5 pair at row 6 cols 4–5 →8. These examples rule out simple global color substitution and a constant replacement color. Candidate submissions that recolored different test motifs (including the upper color-7 square, upper isolated 7, and color-8 objects) all failed; no submitted test transformation is evidence of the correct target.
